title: RTX 5070 Ti object detection: FPS and mAP for 51 models
dek: TensorRT FP16 on an RTX 5070 Ti. D-FINE-X runs 73.0 FPS at 61.5 mAP. Below about 7.5 ms per image, a smaller model stops being faster.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: On an RTX 5070 Ti, speed is rarely the constraint. D-FINE-X is the most accurate model here at 61.5 mAP and still runs at 73.0 FPS. If you need 120 FPS, RT-DETR-L gives 55.8 mAP at 122.0 FPS. All numbers are TensorRT FP16, batch 1, mAP@50-95 in percent.
Fastest models on the RTX 5070 Ti

blocks.caption: Fastest detectors on RTX 5070 Ti, TensorRT FP16, batch 1. Timings include pre and post-processing.

blocks.text: The fastest rows hit a floor. DEIMv2-Atto, the smallest model on the board, takes 7.57 ms per image. RT-DETRv2-R34, a much larger transformer, takes 7.52 ms. Timings are end to end, so below that floor most of the time is per-image overhead, not the network. A smaller model will not get you more frames. Batching or a leaner input pipeline will.

blocks.title: Which model for your frame rate

blocks.caption: Most accurate detectors on RTX 5070 Ti, TensorRT FP16, batch 1.

blocks.text: ECDet-X and DEIMv2-X land within a point of D-FINE-X, at 41.3 and 37.9 FPS. D-FINE-X is both more accurate and faster, so on this card there is no trade-off to make at the top.
